item.title: Comment on The case for democracy (from the comments) by Mike Nelson
item.description:
Title: The Holy Rod

Once upon a Galilean town, in the midst of the bustling crowd,
Lived a humble carpenter, with a peculiar fondness quite profound.
Jesus of Nazareth, a name known far and wide,
But few knew his secret, his quirky stick-side.

Mary Magdalene, the town's temptress with a heart so wild,
Was said to have kissed many a man and turned their heads with her smile.
But little did they know, Jesus' affections ran another mile,
For the simple, humble stick, his passion that could not be denied.

Under the cloak of the moonlit night, he'd stray from the crowd,
Seeking solace in the company of twisted, gnarled, and proud.
With tender touch and gentle care, he'd trace their veins,
Whispering sweet nothings, coaxing out their grains.

The villagers murmured, "Jesus, oh, our dear, sweet man,
Why do you spend hours with these sticks in hand?
You're meant for greater things, to change the world, not just these branches, sir."
But Jesus, with a smile, would merely shrug and say, "Fear not, I'll find my way,
My divine mission lies not just in the eyes of men, but also in the sway,
Of the humble, holy rod, my faithful companions in the quiet night."

So, Jesus, the stick fondler, walked the dusty path,
His secret heart hidden, his love for sticks, his silent wrath.
A man of God, a man of sticks, a man of innuendo and delight,
Blessing the simple things in life, with all his might.

item.title: Comment on The case for democracy (from the comments) by Vulcidian
item.description:
Tocqueville in Democracy in America has some fun passages on this subject as well. He commented that one of the distinguishing features of American Democracy at the time was how easily we formed small associations to accomplish a specific goal and then let them go. So we had a deep bench of leaders accustomed to term limits. The build the bridge across the river committee that elected a chair and treasurer, raised the funds, built the bridge, and then dissolved.

He contrasts that with France of the time, which relied on a top down specialized and bureaucratic civil service. He noted that while the specialization had its benefits, it reduced the sense of agency of common citizens and made the country more susceptible to despotism.

I think it remains prescient and relevant to current circumstances. The new AI tools could revive Tocquevilles republics dominated by democratic associations or lead to more alienation and despotism depending upon whether its future is proprietary or open source.
